analyst_view.overall: Lyon are 13th with 7 points and need a win to push toward the top eight; Lillestrom are 34th with 1 point and close to elimination. Lyon's new coach Carlos Vicens, who replaced Paulo Fonseca, won 1-0 at Lille on Saturday in his first game, built on possession and pressing; this is his first home match and the numbers know nothing about the change. The numbers count Lyon's main absences up front, Lois Openda and Pavel Sulc (Openda is reported back in training but still listed out), and Mata, Morton, Ouedraogo and Kango are also missing. Lillestrom lose Gustav Nyheim to a yellow-card ban on top of Garnas and Bassi. Lyon host Monaco on Sunday, three games in eight days, so some rotation is likely; Austrian referee Sebastian Gishamer (about 4.2 cards a game) is in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (Lyon 1.9) and already take about 15% off Lyon for Sulc and Openda. Likely rotation before Monaco trims Lyon a little more, while Lillestrom's Nyheim ban, which the numbers do not see, slightly weakens their attack, so I shade it to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.0 corners, 8.1 for Lyon, already up for their 38 corners in the last six. Vicens wants possession and pressing high up, which fits a game spent in Lillestrom's half, but rotation pulls the other way, so I stay at 12.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, with referee Sebastian Gishamer close to average (4.2 a game) and both sides' recent bookings already counted. A one-sided home game rarely gets heated, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, 19.4 of them for Lyon. A rotated Lyon side without Sulc and Openda should still dominate but a little less sharply, so I go to about 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target, already up for Lillestrom conceding 30 on target in six games. With Lyon's two main forwards out and changes likely before Monaco, I shade it to about 11.2.
